title: China's Trade Booms, but Iron Ore Slips
section_path: China's Trade Booms, but Iron Ore Slips
section_path_text: China's Trade Booms, but Iron Ore Slips
summary:
Main
By Ulf Bergman
Last week's Chinese trade data confirmed that the country's trade surplus will top one trillion dollars for a second consecutive year, highlighting the continued challenges that many countries face in their efforts to reduce dependence on imports from the world's second-largest economy. Additionally, compared with last year, the one trillion mark was reached earlier, and a new record looks likely. Still, according to data released earlier this week, the Chinese economy is facing renewed headwinds.

children.title: A Mixed Picture for Dry Bulk Shipments
section_path: A Mixed Picture for Dry Bulk Shipments
children.section_path_text: A Mixed Picture for Dry Bulk Shipments
children.summary: According to data from Signal Ocean, just over 208 million tonnes of dry bulk cargoes were discharged in Chinese ports last month. The aggregate was 0.7 per cent higher than in October last year.

children.title: Soft Economic Data Could Weigh on Seaborne Volumes
section_path: Soft Economic Data Could Weigh on Seaborne Volumes
children.section_path_text: Soft Economic Data Could Weigh on Seaborne Volumes
children.summary: As a previous Insights article noted, dry bulk trade flow data is often a poor leading indicator of the Chinese economy. The reverse can still hold, however, and this time around softer economic data may signal headwinds for seaborne dry bulk imports.
